target_customer: Commercial EV fleets that need parking and charging, and property owners with underused charging spots
problem: Fleets lack depots with chargers, while private chargers sit idle at night. Curo leases idle spots to fleets as a virtual depot and handles legal, security, insurance and payments.
business_model: Marketplace taking a margin between site hosts and fleets
product_category: Fleet EV charging and parking marketplace

founders.name: Kieran White
founders.background_notes: Described as Tesla's youngest employee in his YC bio.

founders.name: Andrew Porter
founders.background_notes: Built the marketplace and charging app.

technical_complexity.rationale: A software marketplace integrated with several charger networks and payment flows, with no hardware of its own. Integration with many networks was the main effort.

defensibility.rationale: A two sided supply of host sites and fleet demand could compound, but charge networks and fleet providers could offer similar leasing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: YC states Inspiration Mobility Group acquired Curo. That is the only source; press covers only Inspiration's June 2026 purchase of Electrada assets, a different deal.

market_need_then: Commercial fleets electrifying in 2024 often lacked depot charging, and the YC profile claims customers such as Google, Uber, Zoox and Zipcar and 100 percent monthly growth for four months, all self reported.

branding.domain_note: Uses curocharging.com, a suffix variant. Site is operated by Park & Charge, LLC, so the legal entity differs from the brand name.

identity.voice_and_tone: Practical and B2B; tagline 'park and charge anywhere'

branding.community_and_virality: Partnership announcements with AmpUp, SWTCH, Monta and Emobi. No press about the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: A short name with partner press, but several other companies named Curo exist and nothing shows the brand drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Curo ran a fleet charging marketplace from the Fall 2024 batch, claiming 15 plus states, 5,000 stations and large corporate fleet customers, and partnering with several charging networks. YC says it raised more than 6 million dollars and was acquired by Inspiration Mobility Group, but no press or release confirms the deal or date. The customer and growth figures are self reported, so the strength of the outcome is uncertain.
notes: YC text says raised 6M plus from YC, Blue Bear, Not Boring, Eniac and others, with no round breakdown, so no rounds recorded. VCBacked lists 500K pre-seed in 2024-12 and an ambiguous 13.5M seed entry in 2025-01; both unverified aggregator figures. Kieran White's bio mentions 415M raised, which conflicts and is unexplained. Acquisition by Inspiration Mobility Group is unverified by independent press. The live site makes no mention of an acquisition. Dated competitor search returned undated aggregators. Completeness pass: The 500K pre-seed rests on a single database (VCBacked). The YC page claims 6M plus raised in total from YC, Blue Bear, Not Boring, Eniac and others, so the recorded rounds are a known gap.
